family: The single total certificate-prefix language specified in proof.md and family.py. For actual length N choose B as the least positive integer with B^5>4*N^3. Consider k_plus, the least prime >=B, and k_minus, the greatest prime <B when it exists. Keep the explicit upper-branch exceptional guard. Among eligible prime/order branches choose the lexicographically least (4*k+8*d_t-4*B_t-1,k,t), with r=ceil((N-k)/k), t in {floor(sqrt(r)),ceil(sqrt(r))}, d_t and B_t as in proof.md Sections5,12,14. Read the chosen k actual input bits as lower coefficients of a monic degree-k Q, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, then evaluate the descending-power BK symmetric polynomial on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding and that order. Output0 for N=0 or the explicit failed guards. Output is the constant field coordinate; all prefix bits are included in N, Q is input not advice.
theorem: This fixed total language is in P, hence in NP with empty witnesses. For every sufficiently large integer N=|x| in the full pinned B2 model, C_B2(F_N)>=4*N-L, where L=4*k+8*d_N-4*B_deg-1, B_deg=t*(t+3)/2, and the parameters and sharp dimension are defined in proof.md. Every d_N-dimensional affine payload restriction has degree>=B_deg; this is not asserted for the whole prefix language. The generic degree-sensitive finite gate theorem gives4*m-8*d+min(5*B-1,4*B+1) for1<=B<=d under that hypothesis. The retained same-family gain over the +4 ledger bound is4*B_deg-3. L/N^(4/5)->10*2^(1/5), so C_B2(F_N)>=4*N-(10*2^(1/5)+o(1))*N^(4/5) and liminf C_B2(F_N)/N>=4. The supplied original-threshold loss ratio tends to1/2. Relative to the explicitly supplied two-stage degree reference k_pre in proof.md Section9.1, L/L_pre has limit strictly below19/20. The leading certificate8*(sqrt(a)+1/(2*a^2)) is uniquely minimized at a=2^(2/5) among positive finite k/N^(3/5) limits; no optimality of actual circuits is claimed. The fully specified upper-prime adjacent-order reference F_adj and upper-prime upward-order reference F_up are given in proof.md Sections13,14. At every sufficiently large integer length the current complete losses satisfy L<=L_adj<=L_up. Infinitely many actual lengths have the REFERENCE r_plus=u^2+1; there L_up-L_adj=8*k_plus-12*u-16 eventually, hence L_up-L is at least that value, asymptotic to8*k_plus for the reference difference. Additionally, infinitely many actual lengths N_q=ceil((q^5/4)^(1/3)) for primes q have next-prime p with equal reference block counts. At those lengths L_adj-L>=(8*t_adj-20)*(p-q)=Omega(N_q^(1/5))>0, as proved using PNT and elementary integer-window counting. These compare complete certified losses of DIFFERENT fixed languages, not their actual minimum circuit sizes, and assert no strict improvement at every length.
